topic_name: The Semiotics of Culture and Symbolic Systems

151.question: In the semiotic definition, culture is opposed to entropy as...

options.A: A sphere of the organization of information
options.B: A totality of biological mutations
options.C: A set of independent natural stimuli
options.D: A purely energetic exchange
options.E: The absence of ordered sign relations

152.question: The relation of a sign to the object it denotes is the subject matter of...

options.A: Pragmatics
options.B: Syntactics
options.C: Hermeneutics
options.D: Semantics
options.E: Axiology

153.question: A researcher checks the rules for combining the symbols of a formula, setting their meanings aside. He is working in the field of...

options.A: Iconology
options.B: Semantics
options.C: Ethnology
options.D: Syntactics
options.E: Pragmatics

154.question: The difference in the understanding of a single message by audiences of different ages relates primarily to...

options.A: Textual studies as the establishment of authorship
options.B: Palaeography
options.C: Semantics as a relation to the object
options.D: Syntactics
options.E: Pragmatics

155.question: The introduction of the term "pragmatics" and the understanding of semiotics as an instrument of the sciences are associated with...

options.A: F. de Saussure
options.B: C. Morris
options.C: B. Uspensky
options.D: E. Cassirer
options.E: Yu. Lotman

156.question: In C. Morris's theory of signs, a symbol is related:

options.A: To the object
options.B: Only to the sequence of literate epochs
options.C: Only to the origin of the material of the carrier
options.D: To other symbols
options.E: To the person

157.question: Scholars belonging to the trend of the semiotic study of culture that goes back to Saussure:

options.A: L. Morgan
options.B: B. Uspensky
options.C: Yu. Lotman
options.D: W. Ostwald
options.E: B. Malinowski

158.question: Why does the reform of the rules for wearing beards under Peter I have cultural and semiotic significance?

options.A: Appearance ceases to take part in social communication
options.B: All former rituals retain their unchanged obligatory force
options.C: A feature of appearance acquires an obligatory sign value for the new order
options.D: Human physiology directly changes the grammar of the language
options.E: The reform eliminates the symbolic character of social behaviour

159.question: The formula "culture is a generator of structuredness" means that culture...

options.A: Renounces the semantic organization of the human environment
options.B: Arises only after social development is fully completed
options.C: Replaces any social structure with individual arbitrariness
options.D: Orders the world surrounding the human being and makes social life possible
options.E: Reduces the social world to a chaotic set of experiences

160.question: Indicate the formations classed as secondary modelling systems.

options.A: The native spoken language as a primary system
options.B: The articulatory apparatus as a natural prerequisite of speech
options.C: The unconditioned reflex as a physiological reaction
options.D: Art
options.E: Myth and religion

161.question: In what scope is information understood in cultural modelling?

options.A: It is limited to scientifically verified facts
options.B: It covers only measurements of physical quantities
options.C: It excludes normative and religious content
options.D: It is reduced to the number of letters in a message
options.E: It includes knowledge, values and beliefs

162.question: The primary sign systems of culture are...

options.A: Artistic styles
options.B: Religious mythologies
options.C: Legal codes
options.D: Ritual scenarios
options.E: Natural languages

163.question: Why does learning a foreign language help one to become aware of the sign nature of language?

options.A: The habitual naturalness of speech gives way to the need to master a system of rules
options.B: A foreign language is not connected with cultural experience
options.C: A system of signs arises only when a foreigner is taught
options.D: Language learning eliminates the arbitrariness of the link between word and object
options.E: The native language has a biological nature, while a foreign one has a social nature

164.question: The two-layer structure of a symbol is made up of:

options.A: The unchanging physical action of the object denoted
options.B: The image of the object
options.C: An idea mentally linked with the object
options.D: A single technical algorithm of recognition
options.E: The obligatory etymology of the author's name

165.question: The different interpretation of a single image of a dove in religion and in art shows such a property of the symbol as...

options.A: The complete absence of a common figurative carrier
options.B: The dependence of meaning on the sphere of culture
options.C: The exclusively natural origin of meaning
options.D: The independence of interpretation from context
options.E: The impossibility of intercultural use

166.question: The identification of the language of medics and the language of hippies is based on the criterion of...

options.A: The historical antiquity of writing
options.B: The physical material of the sign
options.C: Belonging to a particular subculture
options.D: The size of the ethnic community
options.E: The degree of genetic kinship of the speakers

167.question: The distinction between verbal, gestural and formalized languages is drawn according to...

options.A: The type of signs underlying the language
options.B: The territory of distribution
options.C: The age of the users
options.D: The historical period of creation
options.E: The professional authorship of the text

168.question: A characteristic of a direct message is...

options.A: A polysemantic form with a fixed meaning and free interpretation
options.B: Meaning as the limit of the interpretation of an ambiguous form
options.C: The obligatory unconscious origin of the message
options.D: The absence of any correlation between form and meaning
options.E: An unambiguous link between meaning and sign form

169.question: Why can even an unambiguous authorial intention become symbolic in a cultural context?

options.A: Every author is inevitably devoid of the intention to convey a meaning
options.B: The material form of the work ceases to exist
options.C: Authorship automatically cancels the link between the work and its era
options.D: It enters a broader space of creative interpretations
options.E: The reader is obliged to repeat only the literal meaning of the intention

170.question: Cultural symbolism as a transformed form of class interests is explained by...

options.A: Marxist and neo-Marxist sociology
options.B: Philosophical hermeneutics
options.C: Spengler's morphology
options.D: Warburg's iconology
options.E: Jungian analytical psychology

171.question: In Jung, a symbol differs from a functional sign in that it...

options.A: Always coincides with a scientific definition
options.B: Does not allow for imagination and associative links
options.C: Merely denotes an already known object
options.D: Exists outside mental and spiritual life
options.E: Expresses an anticipated content that is open to further interpretive thought

172.question: In C. Jung's concept, a symbol is related:

options.A: To the goals and actions of the human being
options.B: Only to a consciously established authorial agreement
options.C: Only to the physical properties of the sign carrier
options.D: To archetypes
options.E: To other symbols

options.A: Only by normative approval by a professional corporation
options.B: Only by rational derivation from a system of scientific definitions
options.C: By deliberate creation to influence social processes
options.D: By spontaneous emergence in dreams and fantasies
options.E: Only by literal repetition of a recognized mythological model

174.question: The "numinosity" of an archetypal image means its capacity to...

options.A: Evoke a strong, vivid emotional response
options.B: Exclude personal experience
options.C: Provide an unambiguous legal meaning
options.D: Preserve the precision of a mathematical notation
options.E: Be fully subject to conscious calculation

175.question: Why is a profound artistic image characterized as ambivalent?

options.A: It retains only a positive characterization of the hero
options.B: It is able to reveal a single archetype in both good and evil, the beautiful and the ugly
options.C: It is devoid of any value-laden expressiveness
options.D: It must belong to two authors at once
options.E: It contains exactly two independently given plots
